emergency.heading: Cyprus emergency number:
emergency.detail: Dial 112 for the police, fire, and ambulance anywhere in Cyprus. Operators speak English. The local line 199 reaches the same services.
notices: Dial 112 anywhere in Cyprus for the police, an ambulance, or the fire service. The local line 199 reaches the same services. Operators speak English.
State general hospitals in Nicosia, Limassol, Larnaca and Paphos have 24-hour Accident and Emergency departments. The general line of Nicosia General Hospital is +357 22 603000.

faqs.question: What is the emergency number in Cyprus: 112 or 199?
faqs.answer: Either. Dial 112 from any phone in Cyprus for the police, an ambulance, or the fire service. It is the pan-European emergency number, free of charge from fixed and mobile phones, and reaches English-speaking operators. The local line 199 connects to the same three services.

faqs.question: Do emergency operators speak English?
faqs.answer: Yes. Greek and Turkish are the official languages of the Republic of Cyprus, but the Deputy Ministry of Tourism says English is widely spoken, and operators on the emergency line speak English, according to NHS Wales. State your location and the help you need as clearly as you can.

faqs.question: Who do I call in Cyprus after a theft, a scam or another crime?
faqs.answer: For an immediate threat, dial 112 or 199: both reach the Cyprus Police. For a theft, a scam or lost belongings that is not urgent, report it in person at a Cyprus Police station and keep the report reference for your insurer. Canada's travel advice for Cyprus warns of card and ATM fraud, so if a bank card is involved, call your bank as well.

faqs.question: Is there a separate ambulance number in Cyprus, or is it 112?
faqs.answer: It is 112. In Cyprus, 112 covers the ambulance, the police, and the fire service from a single call, and 199 reaches the same services, so call and ask for an ambulance. The Accident and Emergency departments of the state general hospitals, such as Nicosia, Limassol, Larnaca, and Paphos General Hospital, operate around the clock.

faqs.question: I lost my passport in Cyprus: who do I contact in Nicosia?
faqs.answer: Report the loss to the Cyprus Police, then contact your country's embassy or consulate as soon as possible. British nationals are served by the British High Commission in Nicosia on +357 22 861100. US citizens are served by the US Embassy in Nicosia on +357 22 393939. Other nationals should check their government travel-advice page for the nearest mission in Nicosia.

faqs.question: What number do I call for a wildfire, a flood or a road accident?
faqs.answer: Dial 112 or 199 for the police, ambulance, or fire service. The UK Foreign Office warns of a high risk of wildfires in Cyprus, particularly from April to October, and winter can bring heavy rain and the occasional flash flood. The fire service also responds to road accidents, floods, and rescue operations. Follow local news and the instructions of your hotel staff.

faqs.question: Which state hospital serves Paphos, Limassol, Larnaca, Nicosia and Ayia Napa?
faqs.answer: In a medical emergency, call 112 and ask for an ambulance. Nicosia, Limassol, Larnaca and Paphos each have a state general hospital with a 24-hour Accident and Emergency department. Their general lines are Nicosia General Hospital on +357 22 603000, Limassol General on +357 25 801100, Larnaca General on +357 24 800500, and Paphos General on +357 26 803100. For Ayia Napa and Protaras the state hospital is Famagusta General Hospital in Paralimni. A GHIC or EHIC gives access to medically necessary state healthcare, but the UK Foreign Office says it is not an alternative to travel insurance.

faqs.question: Is the police number different in Limassol, Paphos, Larnaca, or Ayia Napa?
faqs.answer: No. The same numbers work everywhere in the Republic of Cyprus: dial 112 or 199 in Limassol, Paphos, Larnaca, Nicosia, Ayia Napa, and Protaras alike. Non-emergency reports go to a local police station. For hospital care, four towns have their own state general hospital (general lines: Limassol General +357 25 801100, Larnaca General +357 24 800500, Paphos General +357 26 803100, Nicosia General +357 22 603000), while Ayia Napa and Protaras are served by Famagusta General Hospital in Paralimni.

essentials.advisory: The U.S. State Department lists the Republic of Cyprus at Level 1: Exercise Normal Precautions, its lowest level, in an advisory issued on 1 June 2026 and unchanged when we checked on 9 October 2026. Its Level 2 rating is a separate section on the northern part and does not describe the southern resorts. The UK Foreign Office, whose page was last updated on 14 August 2026, warns that the situation in the Middle East remains unpredictable and that there is a high risk of wildfires, particularly from April to October. A GHIC or EHIC gives access to medically necessary state healthcare, but the Foreign Office says it is not an alternative to travel insurance.

tips.label: Tap water
tips.text: Tap water is officially described as safe to drink: the Deputy Ministry of Tourism says Ministry of Health inspectors and local authorities monitor its quality, and Limassol's water utility states that its supply meets EU standards for potable water. One official handout, the media guide for the 2026 Cyprus EU Presidency, says the opposite, so follow any notice from your accommodation or the local authority

tips.label: Sun
tips.text: Use sunscreen and stay hydrated: June, July and August are the warmest months, according to the Deputy Ministry of Tourism, so cover up, drink water through the day and keep out of the midday sun

tips.label: Mosquitoes
tips.text: Mosquito repellent: worth packing for warm summer evenings outdoors

tips.label: At the beach
tips.text: Many of the busy resort beaches, such as Nissi Beach in Ayia Napa and Coral Bay near Paphos, are lifeguarded in summer and fly warning flags, so check the flag before you swim. The UK Foreign Office warns that there can be strong waves and currents, so take extra care at quieter, unguarded spots. Keep valuables in your hotel safe.

tips.label: On the road
tips.text: Use licensed taxis and confirm the fare or that the meter is running before you set off. If you rent a car, remember that Cyprus drives on the left, speeds are in km/h, and seatbelts are compulsory. Drive defensively, as rural roads can be narrow.

guides.title: What Language Is Spoken in Cyprus? Greek, English and More
guides.summary: Greek is the everyday language of the Republic of Cyprus and 79% of residents speak it best. Greek and Turkish are official, English is widely spoken, and road signs are usually in Greek and English.
guides.html:
Greek is the language of daily life in the Republic of Cyprus: in the 2021 census, 733,732 of 923,381 residents (79%) named it as the language they speak best. Greek and Turkish are the two official languages under the 1960 Constitution. English is not official, but 73% of people in Cyprus told a 2023 EU survey they can hold a conversation in it, and road signs are usually in Greek and English.

This page sets out what the law says, what the census counted, how far English gets a visitor, and the handful of Greek words worth knowing. It is desk research from official and academic sources, covering the government-controlled area of the Republic of Cyprus.

The official languages of Cyprus

Article 3 of the Constitution states: "The official languages of the Republic are Greek and Turkish." In the government-controlled area daily life runs in Greek: only 1,551 residents named Turkish as their best language in the 2021 census.

English held on in the courts and in legislation after independence in 1960. The law that kept it in court proceedings was repealed with effect from 16 August 1989, and the rest of that framework from 16 August 1996. A 2022 constitutional amendment allows English again in the Commercial Court and the Admiralty Court, where a judge may permit it at a party's request.

The Statistical Service asked each resident which language they speak best. The census counted 923,381 people in the government-controlled area on 1 October 2021.

Russian is concentrated in Limassol: 11,176 of the 21,642 people who named it live in Limassol district.

Do they speak English in Cyprus?

Widely. In the European Commission's Special Eurobarometer 540, with fieldwork in September and October 2023, 73% of respondents in Cyprus said they could hold a conversation in English as an additional language. The 2025 edition of the EF English Proficiency Index ranked Cyprus 40th with a score of 537, in its "moderate proficiency" band.

For a visitor that means:

  • Road signs are usually in Greek and English, the Deputy Ministry of Tourism says.
  • Emergency calls: 112 calls in Cyprus are handled in Greek and English, according to the European Commission's 112 information.
  • Doctors: Visit Cyprus says the majority of doctors can converse in English, and that nursing staff speak a range of languages.

Emergency numbers and hospital contacts are on our emergency contacts page.

Cypriot Greek and Standard Greek

What you hear in a village coffee shop is Cypriot Greek, the everyday spoken variety of the island. Standard Modern Greek, the language of Athens, is what children learn at school and what is used for formal writing, the media and politics. Linguists describe the two as living side by side: Cypriot Greek mostly for informal talk, Standard Greek mostly for formal settings.

The difference is mostly sound and vocabulary. One documented example: the word for "foot" is póδi in Standard Greek and pói in Cypriot Greek. A visitor who has learned phrasebook Greek will be understood everywhere.

Place names: why Nicosia is also Lefkosia

Official signs and maps transliterate the Greek names with the ELOT 743 standard, so the spelling on a road sign can differ from the English name on your booking. On street signs the Greek name is on top and the Roman-script version below.

The same rule is why the airport operator writes Pafos International Airport.

Note that ne means yes, which catches out English speakers. The words for what lands on a tavern table are in our Cyprus meze guide.

Minority and community languages

  • Armenian and Cypriot Maronite Arabic are the two languages Cyprus protects under the European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages. Cypriot Maronite Arabic, called Sanna by its speakers, was recognised in 2008 and is tied to the village of Kormakitis.
  • Cypriot Sign Language has been recognised in law since 2006 (Law 66(I)/2006).
  • Turkish is an official language of the Republic. The Turkish spoken on the island is a distinct Cypriot variety.

How this page was compiled

Every figure here comes from a source opened on 17 November 2026. The census numbers are the Statistical Service's count of the language each resident said they speak best, which is not the same as every language they can use. The Eurobarometer figure is self-reported. Nothing here measures how much English you will meet in a particular village.

Frequently Asked Questions

What language is spoken in Cyprus?

Greek. In the 2021 census 79% of residents of the government-controlled area named Greek as the language they speak best. Greek and Turkish are the official languages, and English is widely spoken.

Is English an official language in Cyprus?

No. The Constitution names Greek and Turkish. English is widely used in tourism and business and may be permitted in the Commercial and Admiralty Courts, but it has no official status.

Can you get by with English in Cyprus?

Yes. In a 2023 EU survey 73% of people in Cyprus said they can hold a conversation in English, road signs are usually in Greek and English, and 112 operators answer in both.

Is Cypriot Greek the same as Greek?

It is a variety of Greek with its own sounds and words, used in everyday speech. Schools, the media and official writing use Standard Modern Greek, and speakers of either understand a visitor's phrasebook Greek.

Do people in Cyprus speak Turkish?

Turkish is an official language of the Republic, but in the government-controlled area few people use it day to day: 1,551 residents named it as their best language in the 2021 census.

Why do signs say Lefkosia and Lemesos?

They are the official transliterations of the Greek names for Nicosia and Limassol. Signs follow the ELOT 743 standard, so you will also see Pafos for Paphos and Larnaka for Larnaca.

guides.title: Is Cyprus in Schengen? Status, 90-Day Rule and Border Checks
guides.summary: Cyprus is an EU member that is not in the border-free Schengen area, as checked on 17 November 2026. Documents are checked on flights from Schengen countries and days in Cyprus are counted separately from the Schengen 90 days.
guides.html:
No. Cyprus has been an EU member since 1 May 2004 and uses the euro, but it is not in the border-free Schengen area: as checked on 17 November 2026, the Council of the EU had not lifted internal border controls with Cyprus. Passports or ID cards are checked on every flight between Cyprus and a Schengen country, and days spent in Cyprus are counted separately from the Schengen 90 days.

This page explains what that means at the airport, how the 90-day rule works, which visas are accepted, and where the accession process stands. It is desk research from EU and government sources, covering the Republic of Cyprus. Entry rules depend on your passport, so confirm your own case with the official source before you fly.

Cyprus, the EU and Schengen at a glance

QuestionAnswer
In the European Union?Yes, since 1 May 2004
Uses the euro?Yes, since 1 January 2008
In the border-free Schengen area?No. The European Commission says Cyprus takes part in Schengen cooperation, but internal border controls have not yet been abolished
Passport or ID checked on flights from Schengen countries?Yes
Days counted with the Schengen 90 days?No, Cyprus keeps its own 90 days in any 180
EU Entry/Exit System (EES)?Not used in Cyprus; passports are stamped by hand

What it means at the border

EU citizens need a valid passport or national identity card. The EU's Your Europe portal puts it plainly: you must show one "if you travel between a Schengen country and Cyprus or Ireland".

British citizens need a passport that was issued less than 10 years before the day they arrive and that expires at least 3 months after the day they plan to leave, with at least one blank page for the stamp, according to UK government travel advice updated on 14 August 2026.

Everyone should expect a document check on arrival and departure, including on flights from Greece, Germany or any other Schengen country. Allow for it when you plan a connection.

The 90-day rule: Cyprus has its own count

Visa-free visitors from outside the EU can usually stay 90 days in any 180-day period, and Cyprus counts this on its own. The European Commission's short-stay calculator leaves stays in Cyprus and Ireland out when the Schengen total is worked out.

In practice, for a British passport holder:

  • a month in Cyprus uses none of the Schengen allowance;
  • a month in Greece or Spain uses none of the Cyprus allowance;
  • each limit still applies in its own area, so 90 days in Cyprus in any 180 remains the ceiling there.

UK travel advice says the same: visits to Cyprus do not count towards the 90-day Schengen limit. US, Canadian and Australian advice gives the 90-day visa-free limit for Cyprus without spelling out the separate count.

Visas: what a Schengen visa does and does not do

You holdCan you enter Cyprus with it?Can you enter Schengen with it?
A valid Schengen visa (category C, double or multiple entry)Yes, in place of a Cyprus visa, as long as the visa stays valid for the whole visit and the stay fits Cyprus's own 90 days in any 180. You do not need to have used it in a Schengen country first. Citizens of Türkiye and Azerbaijan are excluded and need a Cyprus visaYes
A Cyprus national visaYesNo. Visas and ordinary residence permits issued by Cyprus are not valid for travel to Schengen countries

Residence cards issued to family members of EU citizens follow different rules. Travellers who need a visa should read the Ministry of Foreign Affairs page for their own passport. Our Cyprus visa and entry page links to the official sources.

EES and ETIAS

EES. The EU Entry/Exit System, which registers fingerprints and a facial image of non-EU visitors, became fully operational in the Schengen countries on 10 April 2026. Cyprus does not use it. The official EES leaflet says that in Cyprus and Ireland passports continue to be stamped manually.

ETIAS. The European Travel Information and Authorisation System will cover Cyprus as well as the Schengen countries. It was not in operation when we checked on 17 November 2026, and no start date had been announced. When it starts, the standard fee is €20 (waived for travellers under 18 or over 70), an authorisation lasts three years or until the passport expires, and the regulation makes ETIAS optional for the first six months. Check the official EU ETIAS site before you travel, and ignore third-party sites that charge more.

Is Cyprus joining Schengen?

It is in the process, and no date has been decided. What is on the record:

  • Cyprus was connected to the Schengen Information System on 25 July 2023.
  • The European Commission carried out a monitoring visit in December 2025 to assess how prepared Cyprus is.
  • A Council working party discussed closing Cyprus's evaluation action plan on 13 November 2026, with the full application of the Schengen rules as a separate agenda item.
  • Joining needs a unanimous decision by the Council. We found no such decision and no scheduled vote.
  • President Nikos Christodoulides said Greece is aiming for Cyprus to join on 1 July 2027, the Cyprus Mail reported on 12 November 2026. That is a target, not a decision.

Until a Council decision takes effect, everything on this page stays as it is.

Which EU countries are outside Schengen?

EU countrySchengen status
CyprusOutside the border-free area; accession in progress
IrelandOutside the Schengen area
Bulgaria and RomaniaFully in since 1 January 2025 (air and sea checks ended on 31 March 2024)
CroatiaIn since 1 January 2023 (air checks ended on 26 March 2023)

So of the 27 EU members, only Cyprus and Ireland are outside the Schengen area. Inside it, several countries run temporary border checks on some routes, so a document check can still happen there too.

Which airport or port you arrive at matters

The Republic of Cyprus treats entry through an airport or port it does not control as illegal. In practice that means flying into Larnaca or Paphos. UK travel advice warns that travellers who enter through Ercan airport in the north can be fined for illegal entry or refused entry or exit. Crossing between the two sides at the official points is a separate matter, covered in our Green Line crossing guide.

Customs, currency and roaming

  • Customs. EU customs and VAT rules apply. Arriving by air or sea from outside the EU, Cyprus Customs allows travellers aged 17 or over 200 cigarettes, 1 litre of spirits over 22% or 2 litres at 22% or under, 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus other goods for personal use worth up to €430 per person, with a lower limit for children under 15.
  • Currency. The euro.
  • Roaming. EU "roam like at home" rules apply in Cyprus, so a SIM from another EU country is charged at domestic prices within its fair-use limits.

How this page was compiled

Every statement here comes from a source opened on 17 November 2026. The accession timetable is the part most likely to change: the last item is a press report of a political target, and no official decision exists. This page is information, not legal advice, and it does not replace the entry rules published for your nationality.

  • UK government: Cyprus entry requirements

  • Cyprus Mail, 12 November 2026: Schengen target date

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Cyprus in the Schengen area?

No. Cyprus is an EU member but internal border controls with it had not been lifted when we checked on 17 November 2026. Documents are checked on flights to and from Schengen countries.

Does time in Cyprus count towards the Schengen 90 days?

No. Cyprus applies its own limit of 90 days in any 180, and the European Commission's calculator does not count stays in Cyprus towards the Schengen total.

Can I enter Cyprus with a Schengen visa?

Republic of Cyprus consular guidance says a valid double or multiple entry Schengen visa is accepted in place of a Cyprus visa while it remains valid, except for citizens of Türkiye and Azerbaijan. A Cyprus visa does not work the other way round.

Is Cyprus in the EU?

Yes, since 1 May 2004, and it has used the euro since 1 January 2008. EU membership and Schengen membership are separate things.

Do I need ETIAS for Cyprus?

Not yet. ETIAS will apply to Cyprus when it starts, with a standard fee of €20, but it was not in operation on 17 November 2026 and no start date had been announced.

When will Cyprus join Schengen?

No date has been decided. The Council of the EU has to agree unanimously. The latest public target, reported by the Cyprus Mail on 12 November 2026, is 1 July 2027.

guides.title: Cyprus Meze Guide: What Arrives, in What Order and What It Costs
guides.summary: A Cypriot meze is one order, priced per person, that brings around 15 to 20 small shared plates. This page sets out the order of service, meat and fish tables, vegetarian and fasting options, and menu prices checked on 17 November 2026.
guides.html:
A Cypriot meze is one order, priced per person, that brings a long run of small shared plates. The Deputy Ministry of Tourism says a full table typically has around 15 to 20 dishes, counting the dips and bread, and that some places serve up to 30. On eight tavern menus read on 17 November 2026, a meat meze cost €22 to €35 per person and a fish meze €30 to €40, and six of the eight asked for at least two people.

This guide sets out what arrives and in what order, what is on a meat table and a fish table, what a vegetarian can eat, and what the bill looks like. It is desk research from official Cyprus sources and the taverns' own published menus, covering the Republic of Cyprus. Prices change, so treat every figure as the price shown on the date given.

What is a Cypriot meze?

Meze is short for mezedes, which the tourism ministry's food guide translates as "little delicacies". The ministry describes it as a variety of small dishes that combine into a feast. You do not choose the plates one by one: the table orders "meze", meat or fish, and the kitchen sends its own sequence. Some taverns also offer a mixed or a vegetarian set. The same dishes that appear as single orders elsewhere on the menu, such as grilled halloumi, sheftalia or stifado, turn up here in smaller portions.

The order of a meze, course by course

There is no fixed national sequence, and each tavern has its own. The order below follows the ministry's Flavours of Cyprus guide, which starts with the olives and ends with fruit.

StageWhat arrivesTypical plates
1Olives, dips, bread and saladCracked green olives with coriander, lemon and garlic (elies tsakistes), tahini, talattouri, taramosalata, hummus, village salad
2Vegetables, greens and small fishGreens cooked with egg, black-eyed beans (louvi), fried squid rings, red mullet (barbouni), octopus in red wine
3Grilled cheese and cured meatHalloumi, lountza (cured pork loin), smoked village sausage (loukaniko)
4Kitchen dishesKoupepia (stuffed vine leaves), keftedes (meatballs), afelia with bulgur pilaf, stifado, tava
5Charcoal and the sealed ovenSheftalia, souvlaki, kleftiko or ofto (roast meat with potatoes)
6Fruit and sweetsFresh fruit, sometimes a sweet pastry or a spoon sweet (glyko tou koutaliou)

The guide places the kebabs and oven meat near the end, after the casseroles. That is why the usual advice is to go slowly on the bread and dips: the heaviest plates are still to come.

Meat meze or fish meze

Most taverns serve one or the other, and the fish version is a different meal, not a variation. The ministry's examples for a meat meze include grilled pork and chicken, sausages, kleftiko, stifado and tava. A fish meze runs through small fried fish, sea bream, cuttlefish, squid and octopus. Pyxida Fish Tavern at Limassol Marina sums up its own as salad, starters, grilled and fried fish, and stewed seafood.

What a Cyprus meze costs

The Deputy Ministry of Tourism's indicative price list for March 2025 puts dinner at a local tavern, meze with a beer or cold drink, at an average of €28. The ministry's rules for catering businesses say displayed prices should already include the service charge and VAT, and its visitor pages describe tipping as at the customer's discretion. For how a meze fits a daily budget, see Cyprus on a budget.

How to order

  • Come as two or more. Six of the eight menus above set a minimum of two people. Pyxida's menu adds a €7 cover charge when a table orders fewer meze than it has people. A solo diner is usually better off ordering three or four single plates.
  • Say meat or fish. A tavern that offers both prices them separately.
  • Allow the evening. Visit Cyprus gives general restaurant hours as 12:00 to 15:00 for lunch and from 19:00 until late for dinner; each tavern sets its own.
  • Ask for the leftovers. The Cyprus Mail reported in April 2023 that waiters increasingly offer to pack what is left on the table.
  • Plan the drive home. The legal limit for most drivers is 22 micrograms of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath (50 milligrams per 100 millilitres of blood). For drivers licensed for under three years, learners and riders of motorcycles, mopeds and quad bikes it is 9 micrograms (20 milligrams in blood).

Vegetarian and fasting meze

A good share of the first plates are meat-free, and a tavern that knows in advance can build a table around them. The table follows the recipes published by the tourism ministry and the Department of Agriculture: a kitchen may cook a dish differently, so ask.

Fasting food (nistisimo) is the other route to a table without meat. The ministry's guide notes that pulses, vegetables and fruit are allowed in Lent, and that on Green Monday, the first day of Lent, families picnic in the countryside on vegetables, olives, bread and salad with village wine. In 2027 Green Monday falls on 15 March (see Cyprus public holidays 2027). The Orthodox calendar also has a fast from 1 to 14 August and one from 15 November to 24 December.

Zivania, the clear spirit often poured with a meze, must be at least 43% alcohol by volume under Cypriot regulations. Commandaria, which Visit Cyprus calls the world's oldest wine still in production, was added to UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity on 10 December 2025.

Where to eat meze

These taverns on Cyprus 365 are built around meze. Each page has the address, hours and what the house is known for.

  • Meze Taverna, Limassol Old Town: a full round of Cypriot and Greek meze.
  • 7 St. George's Tavern, Geroskipou near Paphos: no menu, the kitchen sends the meze.
  • Stamna Tavern, Ayia Napa: a family tavern in one of the town's original stone buildings.
  • Katoi, Omodos: meze in one of the village's oldest buildings.
  • Pyxida Fish Tavern, Limassol Marina, and To Akroyiali: fish meze by the water.

More places are in the restaurant listings, and the dishes have their own pages under Cyprus cuisine.

How this page was compiled

Every figure here comes from a page opened on 17 November 2026: the Deputy Ministry of Tourism's food pages, price list and catering rules, EU regulations for the protected names, Cyprus government publications, and the menus the taverns publish themselves. Nothing on this page was tasted or priced in person for this guide. Menu prices were not confirmed with the taverns and most menus carry no date, so check before you book.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many dishes are in a Cypriot meze?

Typically around 15 to 20, counting the dips and bread, according to the Deputy Ministry of Tourism. Some taverns serve up to 30.

How much does meze cost in Cyprus?

On eight tavern menus read on 17 November 2026, meat meze cost €22 to €35 per person and fish meze €30 to €40. The tourism ministry's March 2025 price list gives an average of €28 for a tavern meze dinner with a beer or cold drink.

Can one person order a meze?

Often not. Six of the eight menus checked set a minimum of two people. A solo diner can order a few single plates from the same kitchen.

Is Cypriot meze suitable for vegetarians?

Partly. Olives, tahini, hummus, salad, grilled halloumi and black-eyed beans are meat-free, while the grill and oven courses are meat. Tell the tavern when you book and ask about stock in the bulgur.

What is the difference between meat meze and fish meze?

They are separate menus. Meat meze centres on grilled pork, sausages and slow-cooked dishes such as kleftiko and stifado. Fish meze is fried small fish, squid, octopus, cuttlefish and grilled fish, and on the menus checked it cost more.

Do you tip after a meze in Cyprus?

Tipping is at the customer's discretion. The tourism ministry's rules say displayed prices should already include the service charge and VAT.

guides.title: Cyprus Airports: Larnaca or Paphos? Buses, Fares and Taxis
guides.summary: Larnaca Airport has direct scheduled buses to Larnaca town, Nicosia and Limassol, plus seasonal shuttles to Ayia Napa and Protaras, while Paphos Airport has them to Paphos, Limassol and Nicosia. This page tables every fare, stop and departure window confirmed from official sources on 9 October 2026, plus the regulated urban taxi tariff.
guides.html:
Larnaca Airport (LCA) has direct scheduled buses to Larnaca town (€2.70 cash by day), Nicosia (€9) and Limassol (€10), plus seasonal shuttles to Ayia Napa (from €13) and Protaras (€15) whose current timetable listed no departures on 9 October 2026. Paphos Airport (PFO) has direct buses to Paphos (€2.00 by day), Limassol (€10) and Nicosia (€18). Polis, Latchi and Platres need a change from either airport. Fares are adult singles as listed on 9 October 2026.

The tables below set those services out, show where each bus stops and give the regulated taxi tariff. This is desk research covering the Republic of Cyprus (the south) only. Where a figure could not be confirmed, the cell says so.

Cyprus airports: which one for your base

The Republic of Cyprus has two international airports, Larnaca (LCA) and Paphos (PFO), both operated by Hermes Airports. A search for an Ayia Napa airport or a Limassol airport leads back to this pair. Our Larnaca Airport guide and Paphos Airport guide cover the terminals, and this page covers the journey onward.

For each base, the table shows whether a scheduled bus runs from each airport without a change, with the adult single fare listed on 9 October 2026. "Change" means no direct service was confirmed, which is not proof that none exists. Still choosing a base? Where to stay in Cyprus compares all eight.

Larnaca town, Ayia Napa and Protaras have a confirmed direct bus from Larnaca Airport only, and the two resort shuttles are seasonal. Nicosia has a Kapnos shuttle from both, at €9 from Larnaca against €18 from Paphos (as of 9 October 2026), and the Paphos one may involve a vehicle change. Limassol costs €10 from either, so pick that flight on price and arrival time.

"Direct" means direct to the operator's stop, which is rarely your hotel. There is no distance column, because operator-published road distances turned up for two pairs only. Kapnos puts Larnaca Airport to Ayia Napa at roughly 50 km along the A3 motorway. For the Protaras resort area it gives 54 to 66 km by road.

Larnaca town. Route 425 is the cheap way into Larnaca: €2.70 in cash by day under the Cyprus Public Transport (CPT) fares in force from 3 August 2026, or €4.70 between 21:00 and 04:00. A notice effective 1 September 2025 put the route on a 30-minute frequency, Monday to Sunday. CPT describes Finikoudes as a 7-minute walk from Larnaca Station. Its older route map shows a Finikoudes stop, but a current one was not confirmed, so plan on the station.

Ayia Napa and Protaras. Kapnos Airport Shuttle prices Ayia Napa from €13 on a page dated 28 June 2026. The same page also calls the fare fixed and describes dynamic pricing, so treat €13 as the floor. On Fridays the first departure is 04:00, not 02:30. Protaras costs €15 (same date) and takes about 65 minutes out and about 60 minutes back. Its stops are on Pernera Avenue and at the McDonald's stop on Protaras Avenue, not at Fig Tree Bay.

Both shuttles are seasonal, and Kapnos's own sources disagreed on 9 October 2026: the June pages describe daily departures, while the current timetable for the route showed no departures available. Check that timetable for your dates before counting on either shuttle. If nothing is running, the fallback is a taxi on the fixed airport schedule described below.

Nicosia and Limassol. The Kapnos shuttle to Nicosia (€9, on an undated timetable seen on 9 October 2026) ends at its Kyrenias Avenue station in Aglandjia, not at Solomos Square, and its 04:45 departure does not run on Sundays. The Limassol Airport Express (€10, timetable valid from 1 July 2026) serves a tourist-area stop opposite St Raphael and ends at Agios Georgios Havouzas station. For public holidays such as Christmas, New Year and Easter, the operator asks passengers to request a revised itinerary. In both towns the onward connection and its fare were not confirmed.

Larnaca local buses that call at the airport

CPT also runs local routes through the airport on the same urban fares, in force from 3 August 2026. Drivers sell single tickets for cash, accepting only coins of €0.05 or more and banknotes up to €20. The cheaper fare needs a plastic Motion card, which costs €5.00 to issue and must be topped up before you board.

Two local buses and two coach services leave Paphos Airport. No published journey time was found for any of them.

Route 612 is the one for Kato Paphos: it serves the Almyra and Poseidonos corridor and Kings Avenue Mall before ending at Tombs of Kings Station. Route 611 serves the harbour from that station. Route 613 runs via Geroskipou to Karavella Station, the starting point for buses to Polis. Pafos Transport Organisation says these two airport lines run year-round without changes.

At night the same page lists a €3.00 ticket, sold only on the bus. Separate wording there refers to an evening paper ticket with a maximum charge not exceeding €3.50, so carry the higher amount if you land late (undated page, seen on 9 October 2026). The last 612 departure from the airport is listed at 01:00.

The Limassol Airport Express charges €10 from Paphos Airport as well (timetable valid from 1 July 2026). Its departures differ from day to day, and the same public-holiday rule applies, so read the operator's Paphos itinerary for your date. The Kapnos shuttle to Nicosia also changes by day:

It is headed for Nicosia and Larnaca, and warns that the journey may include a short stop, a vehicle change, or both. Monday shows three departures (12:00, 18:30 and 21:15). Thursday's last one is 15:30, so a Thursday evening arrival has no listed shuttle. Which Larnaca stop the timetable means, and whether €18 applies to it, was not confirmed.

Polis is the simplest of these by bus: route 613 to Karavella Station, then route 645 to Polis on a timetable that varies by day. Latchi is one more leg on route 622 (Polis, Prodromi, Latchi, Baths of Aphrodite), listed on 9 October 2026 as running from Polis daily between 06:00 and 18:00, so an evening arrival should not count on reaching it by bus the same day.

Kapnos's booking conditions allow each passenger one piece of luggage up to 20 kg and one carry-on up to 8 kg, and each extra piece up to 20 kg costs one adult ticket for the route. CPT's conditions of carriage cover small, non-bulky luggage at the driver's discretion, so a large suitcase on route 425 is not guaranteed a place.

On board, Kapnos's Nicosia timetables say card payments only. Pafos Transport sells one-way tickets on the bus, and we could not confirm whether cards are accepted. Kapnos's homepage and booking conditions offer free cancellation up to 24 hours before departure, while its Ayia Napa page states a €1 fee per ticket for the same notice; later cancellations get no refund (all seen on 9 October 2026). The Limassol Airport Express homepage advertises online booking, but its booking page said the service was coming soon.

Taxis from the airport: fixed fares and the urban tariff

Journeys to and from the airports are priced from a schedule of fixed fares by destination, set by regulation K.D.P. 79/2021 (published 19 February 2021, in force from 1 March 2021). It has separate day (06:00 to 20:30) and night (20:30 to 06:00) fares, and separate columns for taxis carrying up to four passengers and five to six. The fixed fares include luggage and VAT, and the schedule also applies on public holidays. Hermes Airports says the taxi service runs 24 hours a day.

This page does not print those fares: we could not confirm on 9 October 2026 whether the 2021 schedule has since been replaced, and Hermes Airports' public transport page showed no indicative taxi fares to the resorts when we opened it. The schedule is linked in the sources below. Ask the driver for the fixed fare to your destination before setting off.

Rural and interurban taxis have their own tariffs. Their official tariff PDFs would not open on 9 October 2026, so no rural or interurban figures appear here.

How this page was compiled

This page is desk research, and nobody rode these buses for it. On 9 October 2026 we opened each operator's own fare page, route page or timetable PDF, plus the two taxi regulations, and kept only the figures printed there.

Not confirmed: road distances and drive times; most journey times; through fares and connections on journeys with a change; when the seasonal Kapnos shuttles run; which night fare applies on Paphos buses; rural and interurban taxi tariffs; any amendment to the 2021 airport schedule; the current alignment of routes 407 and 430; Limassol Airport Express booking and luggage rules; and whether the undated Kapnos timetables hold for a given date. Fares and timetables change, so check the operator's page before you travel.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which airport for Protaras, Cyprus?

Larnaca Airport (LCA): of the two airports, it is the only one with a confirmed direct shuttle to Protaras, and that shuttle is seasonal. Kapnos Airport Shuttle lists an adult fare of €15 and a journey of about 65 minutes on a page dated 28 June 2026, but its current timetable showed no departures on 9 October 2026, so check before you travel.

Is there a bus from Larnaca Airport to Ayia Napa?

Yes, in season. Kapnos Airport Shuttle's page dated 28 June 2026 lists daily departures from Larnaca Airport to Ayia Napa Square from 02:30 to 23:25 (from 04:00 on Fridays), a journey of 44 to 45 minutes in normal traffic and adult fares from €13 one way. On 9 October 2026 the route's current timetable showed no departures, so check it for your dates.

How do I get from Paphos Airport to Limassol?

Take the Limassol Airport Express, a direct coach from Paphos Airport to Agios Georgios Havouzas station in Limassol. The adult fare is €10 and the child fare (ages 3 to 12) €5 on the timetable valid from 1 July 2026, checked 9 October 2026. Departures differ by day of the week, and the operator asks passengers to request a revised itinerary for public holidays.

How many airports are in Cyprus?

Two international airports serve the Republic of Cyprus: Larnaca (LCA) and Paphos (PFO), both operated by Hermes Airports. Scheduled airport coaches to Limassol and Nicosia start at both, while the seasonal shuttles to Ayia Napa and Protaras start at Larnaca Airport only.

How much is a taxi from Larnaca or Paphos Airport?

Airport taxi journeys are charged from a schedule of fixed fares by destination, with separate day and night fares, under regulation K.D.P. 79/2021 (in force from 1 March 2021). We could not confirm on 9 October 2026 that it is still current, so its figures are not quoted here. The schedule itself is linked in the sources above.

guides.summary: Cyprus has 16 public holiday dates in 2027, 11 of them weekday bank holidays, and Orthodox Easter Sunday falls on 2 May. This page lists every date with its weekday, what official schedules say is closed, and the festival dates confirmed so far.
guides.html:
The Central Bank of Cyprus lists 11 weekday bank holidays for 2027, plus four that fall on a weekend. Plan around Orthodox Easter: Easter Sunday is 2 May 2027, and banks stay shut for five days running, from Good Friday (30 April) to Easter Tuesday (4 May). The eight archaeological sites in the Department of Antiquities schedule, Kourion and the Paphos mosaics among them, are listed as closed on only three days: 1 January, Easter Sunday and 25 December.

Banks are closed on all 16 dates. The Central Bank's calendar also lists every Sunday, and every Saturday for bank transactions, so Easter Sunday and the four weekend holidays (Labour Day, Assumption Day, Christmas Day and Boxing Day) take nothing extra away. Cash machines are a separate matter: Bank of Cyprus, for one, lists its ATMs as available 24/7, including weekends and public holidays (as of 9 October 2026).

Easter Tuesday (4 May) is a bank holiday as well as Easter Monday. Christmas Eve (24 December, Παραμονή Χριστουγέννων) works the other way: it is on the Deputy Ministry of Tourism's holiday list but is not a bank holiday. Six of the 16 dates move every year with Orthodox Easter: Green Monday, Good Friday, Easter Sunday, Easter Monday, Easter Tuesday and Pentecost.

What is closed on public holidays in Cyprus

For state-run sites, the Department of Antiquities publishes two holiday schedules on the government open-data portal: one for museums, one for monuments and archaeological sites. Treat this as the legal baseline, not as a statement of who is trading on a given day. RIK News reported on 18 March 2016 that a court had ruled section 20(a) of the law unconstitutional, and we could not confirm what force the Sunday wording has today. The only tourist-zone decree we located applied from 13 May to 30 November 2015 and has expired, so zone boundaries, seasons and Sunday hours for 2026 and 2027 are unconfirmed. Section 21 does permit daily opening for named categories, among them bakeries, kiosks, vehicle-rental outlets and shops inside hotels, ports and airports.

In the closures table, "Holiday" marks the ten 2027 dates our research matched to the law's list of general-shop holidays (section 23), subject to the tourist-zone provisions. "Not found" means no match, not confirmation that shops open. One date is on the shop list without being a public holiday: 2 January. The tourism ministry's guidance gives the same 18:00 limit for Good Friday, Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve.

Easter in Cyprus 2027: five days to plan around

Orthodox Easter Sunday is 2 May 2027. Good Friday (30 April), Easter Monday (3 May) and Easter Tuesday (4 May) are bank holidays on either side of a weekend when banks are closed anyway, so banks are shut for five days running. Labour Day (1 May) falls on the Saturday in between: it adds no extra bank closure, but it matters for shops.

For shops, the law (as read on 9 October 2026) sets an Easter trading period of the ten days before Easter, with general shops closing by 18:00 on Good Friday and Holy Saturday. In 2027 Holy Saturday is 1 May, and the same section keeps the 1 May holiday when it falls inside that period, so that Saturday is a shop holiday, not an 18:00 close. Easter Sunday and Easter Monday are on the shop-holiday list too, which makes an early close on the Friday and then three shop holidays.

Sightseeing is less affected: the archaeological sites are listed as closed on Easter Sunday only, and the Cyprus Museum on Easter Sunday and Easter Monday. For the weather then, see our month-by-month guide to the best time to visit Cyprus.

The Limassol Carnival runs from 4 to 14 March 2027 and closes the day before Green Monday. That is about three weeks later in the calendar than the 2026 edition (12 to 22 February), so do not carry the 2026 dates forward. The dates come from the Limassol Tourism listing; we had not found a detailed municipal programme as of 9 October 2026.

Two running weekends are also fixed. The TUI Cyprus Marathon in Paphos is on 27 and 28 February 2027, with a 5km Sunset Run on the Saturday and the marathon on the Sunday. The XM Limassol Marathon is on 3 and 4 April 2027, two days after the Cyprus National Day holiday (Thursday 1 April).

Green Monday, Easter and Kataklysmos have confirmed holiday dates but no single organiser, and we had found no local programmes when we checked. Kataklysmos fairs are held in coastal towns, but the holiday applies across the Republic.

The Anthestiria flower festival is the least settled entry. Of the four editions in the Deputy Ministry of Tourism's 2026 calendar, Paphos and Paralimni-Derynia were both dated 10 May, and Larnaca and Amathounta were cancelled.

Public holidays still to come in 2026

Three public holiday dates remain after 9 October 2026 in the Central Bank's 2026 calendar: two weekday bank holidays, and Boxing Day, which it notes falls on a Saturday.

Christmas Eve, 24 December, is not a bank holiday. Under the shop law, as read on 9 October 2026, the Christmas trading period runs from 1 to 31 December, with general shops closing by 20:00, and by 18:00 on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve. That is the law's wording, not confirmed trading hours. On 28 October, 24 December and 26 December the Antiquities schedule, read the same day, lists the sites as open from 8:30 to 17:00.

How this page was compiled

This page is desk research, not a visit report. On 9 October 2026 we copied each date and weekday from the official sources below, without calculating any movable holiday ourselves. Holiday dates come from the Central Bank of Cyprus calendars (2027 dated 6 April 2026, 2026 dated 14 August 2025) and the Deputy Ministry of Tourism's holiday page, whose movable-date calendar covers 2025 to 2029. Closures come from the Department of Antiquities schedules and Law 155(I)/2006. Event dates come from organisers, municipalities and the Deputy Ministry of Tourism's event listings. Four details come from pages not linked below: the tourism ministry's Larnaka Castle page, a Pafos Municipality tender notice, Bank of Cyprus's working-hours page and a 2016 RIK News report.

We could not confirm: the tourist-zone decrees and Sunday shop hours in force for 2026 and 2027; whether the Antiquities schedules apply unchanged in 2027; which official statement on Larnaka Castle is current; any Easter Tuesday closure beyond banks; secondary and technical school holidays; 2027 dates for the events in the second festival table; or the Cyprus Rally's host town. One source error: the Greek version of the Central Bank's 2027 calendar labels 1 May as New Year's Day, while the English version and the Deputy Ministry of Tourism call it Labour Day, which we use.

Dates, opening patterns and trading rules change, so check with the venue or organiser before you book around them.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the Limassol Carnival in 2027?

The Limassol Carnival runs from 4 to 14 March 2027, according to the Limassol Tourism listing checked on 9 October 2026. It closes the day before Green Monday, 15 March, which is a public holiday. The 2026 edition ran from 12 to 22 February, so the 2027 dates are about three weeks later.

When is Easter in Cyprus in 2027?

Orthodox Easter Sunday in Cyprus is 2 May 2027. Good Friday is 30 April, Easter Monday is 3 May and Easter Tuesday is 4 May, and banks are closed on each. With the weekend in between, when banks are closed anyway, that makes five days running. Labour Day falls on that Saturday, 1 May.

When is Kataklysmos in 2027?

The Kataklysmos public holiday is Monday 21 June 2027, across the Republic. That is the bank holiday, not the festival programme: we had found no municipal programme for 2027, including in Larnaca, as of 9 October 2026. In 2026 the Larnaka Municipality programme ran from Friday 29 May to Wednesday 3 June, longer than the holiday alone.

Is everything closed on Sunday in Cyprus?

No, although Sunday shop opening is the one point we could not pin down. The consolidated shop law says general shops are closed on ordinary Sundays, while the Deputy Ministry of Tourism says that in most tourist areas shops and supermarkets are also open on Sundays. Banks are closed every Sunday.

When is the Ayia Napa festival?

The Ayia Napa International Festival last ran from 25 to 27 September 2026, organised by Ayia Napa Municipality. We had found no 2027 dates as of 9 October 2026. The municipality's 2026 announcement is dated 7 September 2026, so check its own notice before you book.

Are museums and archaeological sites open on public holidays in Cyprus?

The listed archaeological sites usually are, and the listed museums mostly are not. The Department of Antiquities schedule marks eight sites as closed only on 1 January, Orthodox Easter Sunday and 25 December. Its museum schedule marks every museum closed on those three dates and most closed on the other holidays too. The Cyprus Museum is listed as open from 10:00 to 13:00 (as of 9 October 2026), except on Monday holidays. Larnaka Castle is listed as open, but the tourism ministry's page says closed on public holidays.

guides.summary: Eleven national forest parks, 17 official trails and three visitor centres in the Republic of Cyprus, set side by side from official sources read on 9 October 2026. Where the official figures disagree or could not be confirmed, the page says so.
guides.html:
The Department of Forests lists eleven national forest parks in the Republic of Cyprus, and three of them (Troodos at 9,147 hectares, Akamas at 7,662 and Machairas at 4,523.6) hold about 92% of the combined area. Trail length is a poor guide to effort: the 14 km Atalanti loop is grade 2, while the 3 km Kalidonia trail is grade 3. Cooking fires are allowed only in the built grills at picnic and camping sites, and camping only at campsites.

Parks in Cyprus: the eleven national forest parks

If you searched for Cyprus national parks, the official designation is national forest park. This table follows the Department of Forests inventory, read on 9 October 2026. Areas are in hectares. In every table here, "Not confirmed" means the official pages we opened did not settle the point. It never means none, zero or free.

Added together, the eleven areas come to about 23,289 hectares. Troodos, Akamas and Machairas account for 21,332.6 of them, leaving under 2,000 hectares for the other eight.

Where the inventory gives more than one declaration date, the table lists each year. The oldest entry is Paedagogical Academy, declared on 27 December 1983. The newest is Akamas, declared on 17 June 2016.

Four of the eleven have their own pages here: Troodos National Forest Park, the Akamas Peninsula, Cape Greco National Forest Park and Athalassa National Forest Park. The declared Akamas park is 7,662 hectares, while our Akamas page covers the wider peninsula. Cedar Valley is not one of the eleven: our page describes it as a valley in the Paphos state forest.

Troodos has the largest published network: 10 trails and approximately 57.6 km, according to the Department of Forests. Machairas follows with 5 trails and approximately 19 km. Cape Greco is described with a 16 km network but no trail count we could confirm, and the 6 trails given for Akamas belong to a description of the wider peninsula. Athalassa's 20 km network is the figure on Visit Cyprus, the official tourism portal (visitcyprus.com, a different website from this one). The four parks not shown had nothing confirmed in these columns.

The Natura 2000 codes identify protected sites associated with each park; their boundaries need not match the park's. They come from the Department of Environment's site inventory and, for CY3000002, the Kavo Gkreko Special Protection Area, from the site list on natura2000.cy.

Troodos nature trails by length and grade

The three trail tables are a selection of 17 officially published trails, not a full inventory. Figures come from the Visit Cyprus trail pages, read on 9 October 2026; where the Department of Forests trail list or the Visit Cyprus brochure differs, the table shows both. The portal grades trails 1 for easy with a gentle gradient, 2 for average difficulty and 3 for high difficulty, described as unsuitable for young children.

Choose by grade first, then by distance. Atalanti is the longest trail here at 14 km and is published as grade 2. Kalidonia is 3 km and grade 3. Persephone is also 3 km but grade 1, as is the 7 km Artemis loop.

Four of the six are linear, so you finish somewhere other than where you parked unless you walk back or arrange a lift. Prodromos Dam to Stavroulia is published in two variants, 4.5 km and 5.5 km. Kalidonia is the trail covered on our Caledonia Waterfalls page.

The Geological Survey Department gives the highest peak of Cyprus as Chionistra summit, at 1,952 m, and the Artemis trail page identifies Olympos as Chionistra. Our Troodos trip planner covers villages, churches and places to stay, and Troodos Mountains gives an overview of the range.

On published grades, Cape Greco is the gentlest of the three areas: Visit Cyprus rates all five trails grade 1, and none is listed at more than 2 hours. Two can start at Konnos, which our Konnos Bay page describes.

Official sources disagree on two rows. For the Cyclops Cave loop, the Visit Cyprus trail page gives 1.7 km and the Department of Forests trail list gives 2.4 km. For Kavos, Visit Cyprus gives 1.2 km and grade 1, while the forestry list gives 2.5 km and grade 2; both give 45 minutes.

Sea Caves to Agioi Anargyroi is linear, so its 4 km is not a circular outing. The name Aphrodite is used twice: the Cape Greco trail is a 2 km grade 1 loop, while the Akamas one is 7.5 km and published as grade 3.

The Avakas Gorge trail was still labelled "Temporarily closed" on its official trail page on 9 October 2026. Check that page before you plan around it; our Avakas Gorge page has the background.

Official sources disagree on four rows. For Adonis and Aphrodite, the individual trail pages give grade 3 and 3 to 4 hours, while the Visit Cyprus trail brochure gives grade 2 and 3 hours. The long Smigies route has three published lengths: 6 km and 2 hours on the trail page and hiking map, 5 km in the Department of Forests list, and 7.5 km and 3 hours in the brochure. Until that is settled, allow water and daylight for the longest figure. Avakas is 1.2 km and 45 minutes on its trail page, 1.1 km in the forestry list and 2 hours in the brochure.

No trail in this selection is a plain grade 1: the lowest published grade is Avakas at 1 to 2, and it is closed. The Blue Lagoon is not one of these marked trails; our Blue Lagoon page covers how people reach it.

Visitor arrangements in Akamas are still changing: a Philenews report dated 20 June 2026 says a revised plan reduces the visitor hubs to eight. We could not confirm which hubs, transport or access charges are in place, so this page lists none.

Visitor centres: opening hours and fees

Three parks have a centre with published hours and a tariff. Both tables use the Department of Forests visitor-centre page, as of 9 October 2026.

CentreParkPublished days and hoursEntry fee, as of 9 October 2026

Kavo Greco Information and Education CentreCape GrecoSeasonal, see the next table€1 for ages 6 to 11; €2 for ages 12 and over

Kavo Greco centre hours by season (Department of Forests):

PeriodDaysHours, as of 9 October 2026

The Troodos and Athalassa centres are published as Monday to Friday only, which matters if your day there falls on a weekend.

Cape Greco is where two official pages disagree. Both give 10:00 to 18:30 from May to October, but Visit Cyprus says the centre is closed on public holidays, while the Department of Forests lists public holidays among its opening days. For winter, Visit Cyprus gives one season, 1 November to 30 April, on weekdays from 10:00 to 14:30. The Department of Forests ends weekday hours at 14:00 and treats April separately. Age bands differ too, as of 9 October 2026: Visit Cyprus lists €2 for adults, €1 for ages 6 to 12 and free entry for ages 0 to 6, and the Greek version of the forestry page starts its €2 band above 12. Confirm before a visit on a public holiday, between November and April, or with a 12-year-old.

These charges are for the centres, not the parks. None of the pages we opened publishes a general admission charge for any of the eleven parks, and none states that entry is free, so that question stays open here.

Forest rules: fires, camping, off-road driving, drones and Lara turtle beach

TopicStatusWhat the source says

CampingConfirmedCamping in the forest only at camping sites
Driving off forest roadsConfirmedDriving a motor vehicle of any type outside forest roads is prohibited by the Forest Law
Aspros Potamos to Toxeftra forest road (Akamas)Listed as closedThe Department of Forests notice says the road remains closed

Lara and Toxeftra beaches, 1 June to 30 SeptemberDescribed in a 2019 government reportNo camping, umbrellas or sunbeds, no people in the area at night, no vehicles on the beaches, no boats entering or anchoring, no fishing except with rod and line

The barbecue permission applies to the built grills themselves. A picnic site is not a licence to light a fire on the ground beside one.

A rough forest road and open ground are different things: driving any type of motor vehicle outside forest roads is what the Department of Forests says the Forest Law expressly prohibits. Separately, the Aspros Potamos to Toxeftra forest road in Akamas is listed as remaining closed in a Department of Forests notice read on 9 October 2026.

The Lara rows rest on a 2019 government report to the Council of Europe and a March 2026 amendment to the Fisheries Regulations (K.D.P. 139/2026). We could not open the current consolidated text, so exact night hours are not restated; our Lara Beach page has the visiting basics, and the signs at the beach are the authority.

For drones, a decree published on 4 March 2026 prohibits all civil and private drone flights over the Republic of Cyprus and within 12 nautical miles of its coast. The official drone portal that hosts it also tells operators to check its geographical zones before any flight, so look at drones.gov.cy for the current position before you pack one. No fine amounts are quoted here, because none was confirmed.

Forest campsites and published fees

Because camping is allowed only at campsites, here are the four forest campsites listed by Troodos Geopark, with seasons and prices as shown on its page on 9 October 2026. Listed does not mean open: the last column gives the latest status we found. The listing's prices are undated, and this is not every licensed campsite in the Republic.

Only Stavros tis Psokas was reported open in summer 2026. The Department of Forests has published notices suspending and then ending the operation of the Platania campsite (in Greek), and press reports described the Troodos and Kampi tou Kalogyrou sites as closed, with no confirmed reopening date for Troodos. Treat the listed seasons and prices as a record, not an offer, and confirm before you plan a night. The Stavros tis Psokas listing shows €1 for one tent and €2 for two people, as of 9 October 2026, without saying whether the amounts add up.

How this page was compiled

This is desk research: we did not walk the trails or visit the centres for it. On 9 October 2026 we read the sources listed below, together with the individual Visit Cyprus trail pages, hiking map and brochure and the Geological Survey Department's Troodos Geopark page. A same-day fact-check added the drone decree, the Lara sources and the campsite closures. Where two official sources disagreed, both figures are shown. We did not add trail lengths together to make park totals.

Not confirmed: general park admission, the exact night hours at Lara, whether the March 2026 drone decree still applies, districts and trail totals for several smaller parks, which Akamas visitor facilities operate, whether each campsite is open and its prices current, and conditions on the ground at the closed road and trail. Prices, opening hours and closures change, so check the source before you travel.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many national parks are there in Cyprus?

There are eleven national forest parks in the Republic of Cyprus, according to the Department of Forests inventory read on 9 October 2026. They range from Agios Nikandros at 25.92 hectares to Troodos at 9,147 hectares. The oldest declaration on the list is Paedagogical Academy in 1983 and the newest is Akamas in 2016.

What are the best national parks in Cyprus for walking?

Troodos has the largest published trail network, with 10 trails and approximately 57.6 km according to the Department of Forests. Machairas is next with 5 trails and approximately 19 km. Cape Greco has a 16 km network where Visit Cyprus rates all five trails in our table grade 1, and Akamas has two 7.5 km loops rated grade 3 on their trail pages.

Is there an entrance fee for national forest parks in Cyprus?

We could not confirm one either way. None of the official pages opened on 9 October 2026 publishes a general admission charge for any of the eleven parks, and none states that entry is free. The published charges we found are for visitor centres and forest campsites, not for entering a park.

What are the turtle rules at Lara Beach?

From 1 June to 30 September, the Fisheries Regulations for the Lara and Toxeftra area prohibit camping, umbrellas and sunbeds, people in the area at night, vehicles on the beaches, boats entering or anchoring, and fishing other than with rod and line, according to a 2019 government report to the Council of Europe. A March 2026 amendment also bans driving on the turtle nesting beaches. The exact night hours were not confirmed.

Can you have a barbecue or camp in the forest in Cyprus?

Only in the places built for it. The Department of Forests fire-safety guide allows fires to prepare food only in specially constructed grills at picnic and camping sites, and camping only at camping sites. Troodos Geopark lists four forest campsites, but only Stavros tis Psokas was reported open in summer 2026.

guides.title: Cyprus Intercity Buses: Routes, Journey Times and Fares
guides.summary: Ten Intercity Buses routes link Larnaca, Limassol, Paphos, Nicosia, Ayia Napa and Protaras, with adult singles from EUR 5 to EUR 10. These tables set out journey times, departures, stops and fares as published on 9 October 2026, plus the district buses that reach Polis.
guides.html:
Fourteen of the 21 possible pairings between the seven main bases in the south of Cyprus are linked by a direct Intercity Buses route, and adult singles cost EUR 5 to EUR 10 as of 9 October 2026. The most frequent weekday link, Nicosia to Larnaca, lists 30 departures each way and takes about 1 hour 15 minutes for EUR 5. Six of the seven gaps involve Polis, reached by district bus from Paphos at EUR 2 by day.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there a direct bus from Larnaca to Paphos?

Yes, Intercity Buses lists two. Route 36 leaves the Nikolaidis Building in Larnaca at 09:00 every day and is published at about 2 hours. Route 46 runs three times each way, Monday to Friday, via Limassol and takes about 2 hours 45 minutes. Both cost EUR 10 in total as of 9 October 2026.

Nicosia to Limassol bus time: how long does it take?

About 1 hour 45 minutes, as published for route 25. As of 9 October 2026 there are 27 weekday departures each way, from Solomos Square in Nicosia between 05:40 and 21:30 and from the New Port in Limassol between 05:25 and 22:00. An adult single costs EUR 6.

How do you get from Ayia Napa to Larnaca by bus?

Take Intercity Buses route 43 from the Ayia Napa Monastery stop. As of 9 October 2026 it lists 16 weekday departures towards Larnaca, timed from Paralimni between 05:55 and 21:15, and an adult single costs EUR 5. The operator's summer 2026 PDF timetable says to add 10 minutes to those times for Ayia Napa stops.

How do you get from Paphos to Polis and Latchi by bus?

Take Pafos Buses route 645 from Karavella station in Paphos to Polis Chrysochous Bus Station. As of 9 October 2026 it lists 17 departures each way on weekdays at EUR 2.00 for a daytime single. Latchi is not in the route's stop sequence, so the last stretch needs a local connection.

Can you get around Cyprus without a car?

Yes, between the main towns in the south. Direct intercity routes link Larnaca, Limassol, Paphos, Nicosia and Ayia Napa with one another for EUR 5 to EUR 10 as of 9 October 2026. The weak points are Polis, Protaras and the Troodos villages, where services are thinner or could not be confirmed.

guides.title: Cyprus Archaeological Sites and Museums: Fees and Opening Hours
guides.summary: No paid archaeological site or state museum in our tables charges more than €4.50, and the Cyprus Museum is free. Here are the fees, summer and winter hours and closing days for 31 places, district by district, as published on 9 October 2026.
guides.html:
As of 9 October 2026, none of the 18 paid archaeological sites, monuments and museums in our tables charges more than €4.50. Kato Paphos Archaeological Park, Kourion, Palaipafos and Limassol Castle cost €4.50, the other 14 cost €2.50, and the Cyprus Museum in Nicosia is free. The main sites open daily at 08:30 and close at 19:30 from 16 April to 15 September and at 17:00 otherwise, shutting only on Christmas Day, New Year's Day and Orthodox Easter Sunday.

How entry fees and opening seasons work

The official visitor pages split the year into two timetables: summer runs from 16 April to 15 September and winter from 16 September to 15 April. Each paid site publishes one standard adult fee with no seasonal rate, and three Larnaca sites add a pensioner price. Almost every site follows one of three patterns.

  • Main sites, open daily: 08:30 to 19:30 in summer and 08:30 to 17:00 in winter, closed only on Christmas Day, New Year's Day and Orthodox Easter Sunday. Kato Paphos, the Tombs of the Kings, Kourion, Apollo Hylates, Kolossi Castle, Amathous and Choirokoitia all work this way.
  • Small sites, weekdays only: Monday to Friday, 09:30 to 17:00 in summer and 08:30 to 16:00 in winter, closed at weekends and on public holidays. Maa-Palaeokastro, Kition, the Royal Chapel at Pyrga and Tamassos are in this group.
  • Museums, fixed hours all year: one timetable in both seasons and a weekly closing day, Monday for the Cyprus Museum and the Paphos and Larnaca district museums, the weekend for the Limassol district museum.

This page covers the Republic of Cyprus only, the government-controlled south. For what there is to see, start with our guide to things to do in Cyprus.

Organised groups of more than 10 people get 20% off at every paid site in the tables. Concessions for children, students or visitors with disabilities were not on any official page we could open, which does not mean none exist.

This is desk research, not a record of visits. UNESCO's World Heritage List supplied the inscription years. Where another official page (a second listing, a municipality or a regional tourism site) disagrees, both versions are shown.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is the Tombs of the Kings entrance fee?

The Tombs of the Kings entrance fee is €2.50 for an adult, as of 9 October 2026. The site opens daily at 08:30 and closes at 19:30 between 16 April and 15 September, and at 17:00 for the rest of the year. It is closed on Christmas Day, New Year's Day and Orthodox Easter Sunday.

What are the Kourion opening hours?

Kourion opens daily from 08:30 to 19:30 between 16 April and 15 September, and from 08:30 to 17:00 for the rest of the year, as of 9 October 2026. The site shuts on Christmas Day, New Year's Day and Orthodox Easter Sunday. Adult entry costs €4.50. The Sanctuary of Apollo Hylates keeps the same hours and is priced separately at €2.50.

How much are Paphos Archaeological Park tickets?

An adult ticket for Paphos Archaeological Park costs €4.50, as of 9 October 2026. The Tombs of the Kings are a separate site at €2.50. We found no official online ticket platform and no statement on card payment, so carrying some cash is a sensible precaution.

Is the Cyprus Museum free, and what are its opening times?

Yes, admission to the Cyprus Museum in Nicosia is free, as of 9 October 2026. Its regular opening times are Tuesday to Friday 08:00 to 18:00, Saturday 09:00 to 17:00 and Sunday 10:00 to 13:00. The museum is closed on Mondays, Christmas Day, New Year's Day and Orthodox Easter Sunday. On other public holidays it opens from 10:30 to 13:00, and on the first Wednesday of every month from 08:00 to 20:00.

Is Limassol Castle open on Sundays?

Yes, from 10:00, but two official listings disagree on when it closes. The castle listing says 13:00 and the Cyprus Medieval Museum listing says 17:00, so plan to finish by 13:00. On Saturdays one gives 09:00 to 17:00 and the other 10:00 to 17:00. Both give Monday to Friday 09:00 to 17:00. Adult entry costs €4.50, as of 9 October 2026.

Is the entry card for Cyprus archaeological sites worth it?

Only on a busy day. The one-day card costs €8.50, as of 9 October 2026, so it beats single tickets once you visit two €4.50 sites, or one €4.50 site and two €2.50 sites. The three-day card costs €17.00 and the seven-day card €25.00.

guides.title: Crossing the Green Line in Cyprus: Rules and Tips
guides.summary: How tourists legally cross the Green Line from south Cyprus: crossing points, passport rules, rental car insurance, currency, roaming, and day-trip logistics.
guides.html:
You can legally cross the Green Line into the Turkish-occupied north as a day trip if you entered Cyprus through the Republic-controlled south, meaning Larnaca or Paphos airport, or a southern seaport. Crossing at an authorized checkpoint is legal and routine, and is done well over a million times a year, though the authorities on the northern side apply their own entry rules and a few nationalities must arrange a visa in advance. What is not legal is entering the island through Ercan airport or a northern seaport first: authorities treat that as illegal entry, which can cause problems if you later try to leave through Larnaca or Paphos.

This guide covers the crossing itself: checkpoints, documents, rental car insurance, what changes once you are across, and the safety rules near the buffer zone. Cyprus 365 covers the Republic-controlled south only (see our Cyprus first-timers guide and things to do in Cyprus) and does not produce itineraries for the north; this guide exists because visitors staying in Nicosia, Paphos, Limassol, and Larnaca ask about the crossing constantly, so it stays strictly practical, rules and logistics rather than a recommendation on your day across.

What the Green Line actually is

The Green Line is the informal name for the UN Buffer Zone, a strip running roughly 180 km across Cyprus, from Kato Pyrgos in the west to Paralimni in the east, with a separate section near Kokkina. In parts of old Nicosia it narrows to a few meters between buildings; in rural stretches it widens to a few kilometres. The line traces the ceasefire positions of August 1974, after that year's Turkish military intervention brought roughly the northern third of the island under Turkish military control. Nicosia, split by the line, is widely described as the last divided capital city in Europe.

UNFICYP, the UN Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus, keeps permanent watch over the zone by vehicle, on foot, by bicycle, and by helicopter. Around 1,000 incidents occur inside it each year, most minor, and more than 10,000 people live or work inside designated Civil Use Areas within it. Decades of near-total absence of hunting and disturbance have also turned much of the zone into an accidental wildlife haven.

The legal framework, in plain terms

The Republic of Cyprus considers the whole island its sovereign territory, including the north, with one legal exception: under Article 1 of the 1960 Treaty of Establishment the Akrotiri and Dhekelia Sovereign Base Areas are excluded and remain under British sovereignty, which matters later because two crossings sit inside them. Under EU law the north is EU territory in principle, but Protocol 10 of Cyprus's 2003 Act of Accession suspends EU law in areas the Republic does not effectively control. Crossing the line is governed by the EU's Green Line Regulation (Council Regulation (EC) No 866/2004, 29 April 2004), which sets the terms for people and goods moving across it.

In practice this produces one clear rule. If you legally entered the Republic through Larnaca or Paphos airport, or a southern seaport (Larnaca, Limassol, Latsi, and Paphos are generally named), crossing at an authorized checkpoint is legal and routine for most visitors, but it is not simply a passport wave: the authorities administering the northern checkpoint apply their own published entry rules, nationals of a few countries (currently Syria, Nigeria and Armenia) must obtain a visa before travelling, and officers may ask about your funds, accommodation and purpose of visit even though you arrived lawfully in the south. What is not legal is entering Cyprus first through an airport or seaport in the north, such as Ercan. UK advice states that entering the Republic through the north means authorities consider you to have entered illegally, risking fines, refused entry or exit, or being blocked from crossing back north. The US State Department separately warns that travelers leaving from Ercan could face difficulty returning to the Republic on a future trip.

There is also a visa-day consequence: the Republic counts time in the north toward your 90-day visa-free allowance, and staying in the Turkish Cypriot-administered area beyond that could see you detained or refused entry back south. None of this affects an ordinary day trip across an authorized checkpoint and back, but the direction of your original arrival in Cyprus matters more than most visitors expect.

The authorized crossing points

There are nine open crossing points along the Green Line. The first opened in April 2003; the two newest, Deryneia and Lefka/Aplici, opened 12 November 2018. Cross only at a designated point; the US State Department is explicit that you should not attempt to enter the buffer zone anywhere else.

Three crossings sit in and around Nicosia: Ledra Street, pedestrians only, the busiest tourist crossing, reopened April 2008 after decades as a barricaded dead end; Ledra Palace, also pedestrians only, a short walk away; and Ayios Dhometios/Metehan, the main vehicle crossing. An EU-funded upgrade there, a third lane each way plus a pedestrian walkway, finished end of January 2026, but hour-long queues were still reported that February, so treat the extra capacity as an improvement, not a guarantee of speed.

The rest sit outside the capital: Astromeritis/Zodhia northwest of Nicosia, Deryneia (also Famagusta/Gazimagusa) in the east, and crossings further west near Kato Pyrgos and Lefka. Two more, Pyla/Pergamos and Strovilia near Dhekelia, sit inside the British Sovereign Base Areas and follow the Base Areas' own rules. The European Commission's reporting on the Green Line Regulation states that at these two points third country nationals other than UK citizens may cross only if they are engaged in a defence related activity or are family members of someone who is. So EU and UK passport holders can use them, while US and other non-EU visitors should not count on it, and the restriction is not signposted. Near Ayia Napa or Protaras, use Deryneia instead. Hours vary by checkpoint and season; see the table below and confirm locally.
