beaches.name: Governor's Beach
beaches.tagline: Dark sand and white chalk cliffs east of Limassol
beaches.summary: A run of small coves below bright white chalk cliffs, with dark grey sand and sheltered pools. On the coast east of Limassol, with tavernas above the shore.
beaches.html:
Governor's Beach sits on the south coast east of Limassol, on the way toward Larnaca. Its character comes from the contrast between bright white chalk cliffs and the dark grey sand and rock below. The cliffs reach down to the water and form a series of small coves and natural pools, sheltered from the wind, that are good for swimming and snorkelling. The shoreline runs for around two kilometres, with the rock formations breaking it into separate swimming spots.

The name comes from the British colonial period, when it was a recreation spot for officials, who are said to have been reminded of chalk-cliff coasts back home. Today the main coves are organised with sunbeds and umbrellas, and a cluster of fish tavernas and cafes sits on the low cliffs above, with steps down to the sand. The smaller coves stay quieter and are good for a calmer swim away from the crowds. The white rock formations against the dark sand make the whole stretch distinctive among the south coast beaches.

What to expect

  • Dark grey sand and rock framed by white chalk cliffs.
  • Several small, sheltered coves and natural pools to swim in.
  • Sunbeds and umbrellas on the main coves; tavernas on the cliffs above.
  • The dark sand heats up in summer, so footwear helps.

Governor's Beach is an easy stop on the Limassol-to-Larnaca coast. Combine it with the Limassol sights, such as Ancient Kourion and Kolossi Castle, or with the long, shallow Lady's Mile Beach west of the city. The Larnaca seafront beaches, including Finikoudes Beach, lie further east.

photo.alt: White rocks at Governor's Beach, Cyprus

beaches.name: Konnos Bay
beaches.tagline: Sheltered cove between Protaras and Cape Greco
beaches.summary: A small, sheltered cove ringed by limestone cliffs near Cape Greco. Clear, calm water and pale sand make it one of the most photogenic beaches in the south.
beaches.html:
Konnos Bay is a compact cove of pale sand tucked into the headland between Protaras and Cape Greco. Limestone cliffs and pine slopes wrap around the bay, sheltering it from wind and giving the water an unusually clear, calm character. It is one of the most photographed small beaches in the Republic of Cyprus, and it carries Blue Flag status. The pale sand and the steep green slopes give it a postcard look that draws steady crowds in summer.

The cove sits inside the Cape Greco National Forest Park, a protected Natura 2000 area that runs to several hundred hectares, so the backdrop stays green and largely undeveloped. The calm water is good for swimming and snorkelling around the rocky edges, and small boats and pleasure cruisers sometimes anchor offshore. Sunbeds, umbrellas and a beach kiosk operate in season, but the bay is small and fills quickly, so an early start helps, and the access road down to it is steep with limited parking at the top.

Visiting Konnos Bay

  • Blue Flag cove inside the Cape Greco National Forest Park.
  • Sunbeds, umbrellas and a seasonal kiosk on the sand.
  • A steep access road leads down to the beach; parking is limited.
  • Clear water and rocky edges make it good for snorkelling.

Konnos is an easy stop on the way to the walking trails, sea caves and viewpoints of Cape Greco. It pairs well with a Protaras day at Fig Tree Bay or Sunrise Beach, and the lively beaches of Ayia Napa sit just to the west.

facts.label: Parking
facts.value: Small lot at the top; limited and busy in summer

photo.alt: Konnos Bay, Cyprus

beaches.name: Lady's Mile Beach
beaches.tagline: Long, shallow flat-sand beach by Akrotiri
beaches.summary: A long, flat stretch of dark sand along the Akrotiri peninsula near Limassol, with very shallow water. Beach tavernas, space to spread out and a nearby salt lake.
beaches.html:
Lady's Mile is a long, straight beach running down the eastern side of the Akrotiri peninsula, just south of Limassol. It stretches for several kilometres along flat ground, with dark grey to golden sand and water that stays very shallow a long way out, which makes it easy and reassuring for families and small children. The length means there is almost always space to spread out, even in summer.

The beach lies on the Akrotiri area near the British base, and inland sits the Akrotiri Salt Lake, a wetland of European importance where flamingos and other migrating birds gather in winter. Several beach tavernas and cafes are spread along the shore, some with sunbeds, water inflatables and games for children, so families can settle in for the day. Lifeguards are stationed along parts of the beach through the main season. The access road is largely unpaved, so expect a dusty drive in, and the shallowest, warmest water is at the southern end where the sand turns golden.

Good to know

  • Very shallow water and a long, flat beach suited to families.
  • Beach tavernas, sunbeds and some with children's facilities.
  • Lifeguards on parts of the beach during the main season.
  • The nearby Akrotiri Salt Lake draws flamingos in winter.

Lady's Mile pairs well with the Limassol sights inland, including Kolossi Castle and Ancient Kourion, and the old town around Limassol Castle. For a different kind of beach in the same district, the chalk-cliff coves of Governor's Beach lie east of the city.

facts.label: Parking
facts.value: Informal parking along the beach (unpaved road)

beaches.name: Landa Beach
beaches.tagline: Calm, soft-sand bay between Nissi and Makronissos
beaches.summary: A gently shelving bay of fine sand west of Ayia Napa, between Nissi and Makronissos. Calm shallow water makes it good for families. Blue Flag beach.
beaches.html:
Landa Beach sits about midway between Nissi Beach and Makronissos Beach, a few kilometres west of central Ayia Napa. It is a roughly 400-metre bay of fine, soft sand with gently shelving, shallow water, and it holds Blue Flag status. The name means pond in the local dialect. The calm entry and the easy-going setting make it a quieter family alternative to the busier, louder beaches nearer the centre of town, and the surrounding scenery keeps the mood relaxed.

The beach is organised with sunbeds, umbrellas and watersports in season, and a coastal path links it to the neighbouring bays so you can walk between them. Lifeguards are stationed through the summer months, and the gentle, shallow water gives parents room to relax. Because it is set back from the main Ayia Napa nightlife, Landa keeps a calmer, more relaxed mood, especially in the morning before the day-trippers arrive and the sunbeds fill up. It is a sensible base for a slower beach day, with the option to walk to the livelier beaches when you want more going on.

Good to know

  • Blue Flag beach with lifeguards during the summer season.
  • Soft sand and shallow water suited to families and children.
  • Sunbeds, umbrellas, showers and watersports available in season.
  • A coastal path links Landa with the neighbouring beaches.

Landa works well as part of a beach-hopping day along the Ayia Napa coast, between the lively Nissi Beach and the three coves of Makronissos Beach. The cliffs and walking trails of Cape Greco lie a short drive to the east, on the way to Protaras.

facts.label: Parking
facts.value: Parking near the beach; payment machines at the municipal Lanta parking area

photo.alt: Landa Beach, Cyprus

beaches.name: Lara Beach
beaches.tagline: Wild turtle-nesting beach on the Akamas
beaches.summary: An undeveloped Akamas beach and protected turtle-nesting site, reached by rough track. No facilities, no sunbeds, usually a 4x4 to get there.
beaches.html:
Lara Beach lies on the western side of the Akamas peninsula, north of Coral Bay and Paphos. It is one of the few entirely undeveloped beaches left on this coast: a wide, sweeping bay of pale sand with no sunbeds, no beach bar and no paved access. The rough dirt track that leads to it normally needs a 4x4, and that inaccessibility is exactly what has protected it.

Lara is one of the most important sea-turtle nesting sites in the Mediterranean. Loggerhead and green turtles come ashore here to nest, and the Cyprus Department of Fisheries and Marine Research has run a conservation hatchery on the beach since 1978, protecting at-risk eggs and releasing hatchlings to the sea. Nesting runs through the summer, with most activity at night, and parts of the beach may be roped off or closed to protect nests. The wider Akamas is a protected landscape, so the bay stays free of the sunbeds, bars and buildings that line beaches elsewhere on the coast.

Visiting responsibly

  • Access is by a rough track; a 4x4 is normally needed.
  • There are no facilities, shade, sunbeds or kiosks. Bring water and sun cover.
  • Keep off marked nesting areas and follow any signs from the hatchery.
  • The 2020 government report gives restrictions from 1 June to 30 September: no umbrellas, sunbeds, tents or caravans, and no staying overnight, starting an hour before sunset. Check current rules and signs before visiting.

Lara works well alongside other Akamas trips: Avakas Gorge is nearby, though its walking trail is temporarily closed, and the Blue Lagoon on the peninsula's north coast is reached by boat from Latchi. For an easy, full-service beach day in the area, head back south to Coral Bay.

facts.label: Parking
facts.value: Rough track and informal parking; 4x4 recommended

photo.alt: Lara Beach, Cyprus

beaches.name: Mackenzie Beach
beaches.tagline: Larnaca's lively beach by the airport
beaches.summary: A long Larnaca beach near the airport, with calm shallow water and a strip of bars, cafes and clubs. Planes pass low overhead. A Blue Flag beach.
beaches.html:
Mackenzie Beach runs along the coast just south of central Larnaca, near the airport and the site of the old airfield. It is a roughly one-kilometre strip of fine brown and beige sand with calm, clear, shallow water, and it holds Blue Flag status. Its best-known quirk is the aircraft: Larnaca International Airport is right beside it, so planes pass low overhead as they come in to land, which plane-spotters and photographers come specifically to see.

Mackenzie has a livelier, more social feel than the central seafront. The strip behind the sand is packed with beach bars, cafes, restaurants and clubs, some of which stay busy into the evening and count among the area's better-known nightspots. The beach itself has sunbeds, umbrellas and watersports in season, and the calm, shallow water still works for a daytime swim. Lifeguards are on duty through the main season. It is popular with a younger crowd, so it picks up in the afternoon and evening, while mornings stay quieter.

What to expect

  • Blue Flag beach with calm, shallow water and fine sand.
  • Bars, cafes, restaurants and clubs along the strip behind the sand.
  • Sunbeds, umbrellas, showers and watersports in season.
  • Planes pass low overhead on approach to Larnaca airport.

Mackenzie is an easy walk or short drive from the central Finikoudes Beach along the seafront. The rest of Larnaca's sights are close: the Church of Saint Lazarus in the old town and the Larnaca Salt Lake, which draws flamingos in winter, are both nearby.

facts.label: Parking
facts.value: Free and paid parking near the strip

photo.alt: Mackenzie Beach, Cyprus

beaches.name: Makronissos Beach
beaches.tagline: Three sheltered golden coves west of Ayia Napa
beaches.summary: Three linked coves of fine golden sand on the Makronissos peninsula, with calm shallow water. Quieter than central Ayia Napa and a Blue Flag beach.
beaches.html:
Makronissos Beach lies on the peninsula of the same name, a short drive west of central Ayia Napa. It is made up of three small coves of fine golden sand, separated by low rock formations, that together run to roughly 350 metres. The water is calm and shallow across all three bays, and the layout gives the beach a more sheltered, family feel than the busier strips closer to town. It holds Blue Flag status and stays a little quieter than the Ayia Napa beaches nearer the centre.

The central cove is the most organised, with sunbeds, umbrellas and watersports, while the side bays are quieter and good for a calmer swim. A coastal path runs along the shore and links Makronissos with the neighbouring beaches, so you can walk between the bays. The Makronissos tombs, a small rock-cut ancient burial site, sit just inland from the beach and are easy to fold into a beach day. Lifeguards are on duty during the main season, and the sheltered layout keeps the water calm even when the wind picks up.

What to expect

  • Blue Flag beach with three sheltered coves of golden sand.
  • Sunbeds, umbrellas, showers, toilets and watersports on the main cove.
  • Calm, shallow water suited to families and younger children.
  • The Makronissos rock-cut tombs sit a short walk inland.

Makronissos pairs naturally with the nearby Landa Beach and the larger Nissi Beach along the same stretch of coast. For a change of scene, the family beaches of Protaras, such as Fig Tree Bay, are a short drive east.

facts.label: Parking
facts.value: Free and paid parking near the beach

photo.alt: Makronissos Beach in Ayia Napa, Cyprus

beaches.name: Nissi Beach
beaches.tagline: Ayia Napa's white-sand bay with a wade-out islet
beaches.summary: Ayia Napa's best-known beach: soft white sand, shallow turquoise water and a small islet you can reach on foot across a sandbar. Lively in summer, Blue Flag.
beaches.html:
Nissi Beach runs along its own cove on the western edge of Ayia Napa, about 600 metres of fine white sand against shallow, clear water. The beach takes its name from the small islet (nissi means island in Greek) just offshore, which you can reach on foot through knee-deep water when a natural sandbar forms. That sandbar, the gentle entry and the pale sand are what put Nissi on most lists of Cyprus beaches.

It is a busy, organised beach. Sunbeds and umbrellas cover much of the sand in high season, watersports operators run jet skis and inflatables, and beach bars play music through the afternoon, so the mood is social rather than quiet. The water stays shallow a good way out, which suits families and weaker swimmers, though the crowds and the party reputation mean early mornings are the calmest time to come. Daytime beach parties run here through the summer, drawing a younger crowd, while the western end of the cove tends to stay a little quieter.

What to know before you go

  • Blue Flag beach with lifeguards on duty through the summer season.
  • Sunbeds, umbrellas, showers, toilets and beach bars line the sand.
  • Free public access; paid parking and side-street parking nearby.
  • Walk to the islet only when the sandbar is exposed and the water is calm.

Nissi sits a short drive from the quieter Landa Beach and the three sheltered coves of Makronissos Beach to the west. For calm, family swimming away from the music, the sheltered Konnos Bay near Protaras is an easy day trip, and the headland walks of Cape Greco are close by.

beaches.name: Petra tou Romiou (Aphrodite's Rock)
beaches.tagline: Swimming and sunsets below the legendary sea stack
beaches.summary: The pebble beach below Aphrodite's Rock, on the Paphos-Limassol coast road. Striking sea stacks and deep, often lively water. Strong on scenery, less so on swimming.
beaches.html:
Petra tou Romiou, widely known as Aphrodite's Rock, is the cluster of sea stacks that rise from the water on the southwest coast of Cyprus, in the Paphos district. In legend this is the birthplace of Aphrodite, the goddess of love, which is why the site appears on so many Cyprus itineraries. The beach below is pebble rather than sand, and the rocks make a dramatic backdrop, especially at sunset.

This is more a scenic stop than a classic swimming beach. The water is deep and can be rough, the shore is large pebbles, and there are no sunbeds or watersports on the beach itself. A viewpoint above the road, a pedestrian underpass down to the shore, parking and a tourist pavilion with a cafe make it easy to visit. Local lore says swimming around the rock brings beauty or good fortune, though the swell often makes that unwise.

What to know

  • Pebble beach with deep water that is often choppy.
  • Parking, a viewpoint and a pedestrian underpass to reach the shore safely.
  • No sunbeds, lifeguards or watersports on the beach.
  • Best at sunset for photographs; bring sandals for the pebbles.

Petra tou Romiou sits on the B6 coast road and combines well with the Paphos sights to the west, such as Paphos Archaeological Park and the Tombs of the Kings, or with the Limassol-side ruins of Ancient Kourion to the east. For a swimmable beach in the same area, head to Coral Bay north of Paphos.

beaches.name: Sunrise Beach
beaches.tagline: Central Protaras family beach with pale sand
beaches.summary: A sandy, family-friendly beach on the central Protaras strip, with calm shallow water and full facilities. Sunbeds, watersports and dining close by. A Blue Flag beach.
beaches.html:
Sunrise Beach sits on the central Protaras strip, just along the coast from Fig Tree Bay. It is a sandy, gently shelving beach with calm, shallow water, which makes it an easy family choice, and it holds Blue Flag status. As the name suggests, the east-facing shore is a good spot to catch the early sun over the sea, and it shares its name with a long-standing hotel set just behind the beach.

The beach is fully organised: sunbeds and umbrellas cover much of the sand in season, watersports operators run from the shore, and a line of hotels, tavernas and cafes sits just behind. The calm, clear water is good for swimming and paddling, and rockier patches at the edges hold reef fish for snorkellers, so it doubles as a gentle introduction to snorkelling for children. Lifeguards are on duty in the main season, and there are diving schools and family activities such as mini-golf nearby. Like the rest of Protaras, it is busy in summer and calmest early in the day.

Planning your visit

  • Blue Flag beach with calm, shallow water for families.
  • Sunbeds, umbrellas, showers, toilets and watersports on the sand.
  • Hotels, tavernas and cafes line the road behind the beach.
  • East-facing shore is good for an early-morning swim.

Sunrise Beach is steps from the rest of the Protaras strip, including Fig Tree Bay and, a short drive south, the sheltered Konnos Bay and the trails of Cape Greco. The beaches of Ayia Napa, such as Nissi Beach, lie a little further west along the coast.
